title: Compatibility contract and migration play for legacy sync vs async endpoints
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Define a compatibility contract and stepwise migration requirements for customers using legacy synchronous and asynchronous endpoints (legacy-sync, legacy-async, longpoll-based transports) into the unified inference API. This document is a product-facing PRD that clarifies acceptance criteria, scope changes since the initial consolidation plan, explicit mapping rules, SDK guidance, telemetry gates, and rollback criteria for a staged sunset.

Background: Multiple customers continue to rely on old synchronous (blocking generate) and asynchronous (longpoll/queue) transports. The previous consolidation artifacts covered broad timelines but lacked a deterministic compatibility mapping and concrete SDK adaptation requirements for common client patterns (blocking request/response, server polled job status, webhook callbacks). Engineering requires authoritative mappings and test conditions to implement routing fallbacks and a compatibility shim for the Dedicated and Hosted fleets.

Problem: Without a precise contract customers continue to see integration regressions during migrations: missing headers, differences in streaming framing, poll-backoff semantics, and webhook delivery edge cases. Those regressions increase support load and risk for high-volume customers during the sunset window.

This ticket produces the product-side contract (behavioral mapping + acceptance tests) and acceptance criteria that the platform/SDK teams can implement and validate prior to declaring end-of-life dates for legacy transports.
goals: Deliver a deterministic compatibility matrix that maps every legacy endpoint verb/response shape to the unified API behavior
Specify SDK guidance and code recipes for client authors to convert blocking and longpoll patterns with minimal code change
Define telemetry gates, error budgets, and rollback criteria for phased rollout
Produce explicit acceptance tests (behavioral) for eng to validate shim/routing behavior in Hosted and Dedicated
non_goals: Rewriting customer client libraries—this ticket provides guidance not customer migrations
Full automation of every third-party integration (partners with bespoke transports)
scope: Legacy async patterns: longpoll /v0/jobs, webhook callbacks for job completion
Compatibility shim behavior in Hosted API and routing policy in Dedicated; Private to receive guidance docs only
SDK change lists and sample snippets for JS and Python clients
scope_changes: Removed: automatic migration of partner webhooks (will be manual-assist) — added to partner support backlog
Added: acceptance criteria for request replay idempotency in async-to-sync conversion
Clarified: Dedicated routing fallback must respect customer-configured model pinning
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral mapping document signed off by Eng, DX, Security — merged to repo docs
Shim passes end-to-end conformance tests: 1000 synthetic legacy requests with 99.9% parity in status codes and error classes vs expected mapping
Streaming equivalence: clients using legacy streaming framing receive coherent token stream under unified streaming (ordering, chunk boundaries) for 99% of test cases
Async poll semantics: jobs created via legacy async carry identical job ids and final artifact URLs when routed to unified job API in 99.5% of tries
SDK recipes (JS + Py) published with example PRs and migration checklist; each SDK has at least one integration test exercising a migrated flow
Telemetry gates emitted: per-customer migration metric, failure rate, and increased support-ticket alerts wired into Console dashboards
Security review completed with remediation items tracked and closed
migration_steps: Publish compatibility matrix and API mapping RFC for internal review (product & eng) — week 0
Implement routing shim prototype in staging that translates legacy sync/async calls to unified endpoints — week 1–3
Create synthetic conformance harness that replays customer traces and verifies behavioral parity — week 2–4
Publish SDK migration recipes and sample code, open PRs to reference SDK repos — week 3
Run canary: enable shim for 5% of traffic for low-risk customers, monitor gates — week 5
Expand canary to 25% and validate telemetry; agree on migration windows with high-volume customers — week 6–7
Open opt-in migration program and shared status board for customers to enroll — week 8
Begin scheduled customer migrations and start sunset notice clock for unenrolled customers after 12 weeks of opt-in window
compatibility_matrix: Legacy POST /v0/generate -> Unified POST /v1/unified/generate: map 'prompt' to 'input', preserve 'stop' semantics, translate 'max_tokens' to 'max_output_tokens'

Legacy /v0/completions streaming -> Unified streaming (SSE/HTTP2): wrap legacy framing tokens into 'chunk' envelope and maintain order; provide fallback header X-Compat-Mode:streaming when strict mode required
Legacy /v0/jobs POST -> Unified /v1/jobs.create: map job scheduling params, preserve job-id in X-Compat-Job header for idempotency
Legacy job poll /v0/jobs/{id}/status -> Unified /v1/jobs/{id}: preserve status codes PENDING/RUNNING/FAILED/SUCCEEDED and expose 'artifact_url' field for artifacts
Webhook callback differences: legacy delivered raw JSON -> compatibility shim will POST to customer webhook with X-Compat-Webhook header and legacy payload shape for 60 days post-migration
telemetry_gates: Gate 1 (Canary): error_rate_legacy_shim <= 0.5% over 1h window for 24h before expansion
Gate 2 (Bulk): customer_seen_failures <= 0.2% and no increase in support tickets attributed to migration within 7d
Gate 3 (Rollback trigger): any single customer experiences >1.5% request loss or >2x latency increase vs baseline — immediate rollback for that customer
Gate 4 (Final EOL): After 12 weeks of opt-in window, aggregate error budget for all remaining routed customers must be <0.1% for 30 days
rollout_plan: Phase A: Internal staging validation and Eng + DX sign-off
Phase B: Low-risk canary (5% traffic), 72h monitoring and gates review
Phase C: Extended canary (25%), targeted customer invitations and documented migration windows
Phase D: Opt-in migration program with dedicated SE support for enterprise customers
Phase E: Gradual cutoff for unenrolled customers with repeated notices (30d, 14d, 7d, 48h) and final automated reroute to a limited-compat mode for 7 days before hard disable
notes: Decision: we will not attempt to preserve non-standard vendor headers beyond X-Compat-*; partners requiring special mapping will be handled via support-assisted migrations
Tradeoff: maintaining a compatibility shim increases short-term complexity in routing and testing but significantly reduces customer migration friction
Follow-up action: schedule a joint tech-review with Dedicated ops to verify model-pinning behavior and SLA implications before canary
